memory_boundary: Memory-only structural leads; no external search, Evidence search, class-rule lookup, flag-rule lookup, society ranking or detention-case verification.

leads.memory: Classification is a private technical-rule/status system distinct from flag-state statutory certification, even though the same survey organization may perform delegated statutory work; research should not collapse the two authorities into one label.

Flag administrations can delegate parts of statutory survey and certification to recognized organizations, creating a principal-delegate chain whose scope and oversight matter separately from class membership.

Class involvement begins before delivery through rule selection, plan/design approval, material/equipment certification and construction surveys; newbuilding class is therefore embedded in yard/design/supplier workflows.

Vessels move through recurring annual/intermediate/special and machinery or docking-related survey windows; survey due dates create a maintenance and availability calendar even when no casualty occurs.

Survey findings may leave conditions, recommendations or due items that require repair, inspection or documentation by a deadline; class status therefore has intermediate states rather than only valid/invalid.

Grounding, collision, machinery failure or structural damage can trigger class attendance and repair approval before normal trading resumes, connecting casualty response directly to technical certification.

Overdue surveys, unresolved serious conditions or other rule failures can lead to suspension/withdrawal; reinstatement generally requires closing specified technical or survey gaps, making class status a real deployability gate.

Changing classification society involves transfer of technical history, outstanding recommendations and survey status; a class change is not simply a new logo and can be scrutinized by counterparties.

Reflagging can require statutory documentation and delegated-survey transitions in addition to registry changes, so flag transfer can temporarily create certification and administrative work even if the vessel is unchanged physically.

Port-state inspections can identify deficiencies and in serious cases restrict sailing until rectified; local inspection outcomes can therefore convert compliance state into delay and effective-capacity loss.

A trading vessel carries a portfolio of statutory/class-related certificates and records with different scopes and expiries; commercial readiness depends on the portfolio being coherent, not one master certificate.

Insurers, lenders, charterers, terminals and buyers may use class/statutory status as screening or covenant inputs, so technical certification can propagate into financing and market access beyond regulator enforcement.

Class survey is sampled/scoped oversight rather than continuous operation of the ship; owner/manager maintenance and disclosure responsibilities remain distinct, an important caution against treating class as a blanket guarantee.
The atlas effective-capacity concept extends to certification: a physically operable ship with lapsed or restricted class/statutory status may be commercially unavailable.
Regulation-as-supply works partly through survey, retrofit and certificate deadlines that bunch drydock or repair demand and can remove vessels temporarily from service.
The P004 repair/conversion ecosystem is constrained by survey attendance, approved repair scope, testing and documentation before technical status is restored.
The P003 insurance and atlas capital-provider layers should preserve class/status dependencies because coverage, covenants or transaction diligence may react to technical status changes.
Design and machinery approval overlap P004's technical-supply/design topology; P011 retains only the class/status institutional angle.
The general statement that regulation changes effective supply already exists in the atlas and is not a new lead here.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Ranking societies by quality, share or current reputation requires Evidence.
Exact intervals, notation rules and editions are precision-fragile.
Delegation scope varies and needs authoritative flag documents.
Exact inspection regimes, lists and cases require source-first Evidence.

method_observation.observation: Recall is high-yield when class/statutory compliance is modeled as a state-transition chain tied to surveys and counterparties; it degrades when reduced to society rankings, rule numbers or detention lists.
